Author beats user agent at any specificity, so the script was correct all along -- it set hidden on 18 cards and the browser ignored it. The counter was never evidence about the PAGE, it was evidence about the LOOP, which is exactly why two control-responded audits cleared it. Now the count is read back from what is actually visible, so break the CSS again and the counter reads 24: wrong about the filter, still true about the page, and the new gate fails the build. issues.title: 'Lot of headline text are showing as cut in bottom'
issues.note: FIXED, and THE OWNER WAS LITERALLY RIGHT. There were TWO defects. (1) The gradient fell 65.2 luminance units across a glyph, worst on descenders, making letters LOOK cut; now 14.3. (2) A SECOND, GENUINELY LITERAL CUT that the forensic audit could not have found and that I twice told the owner did not exist: background-clip:text paints only INSIDE the element box, and clipped text has no fallback colour, so ink below the box is drawn with NOTHING. Measured missing ink: /privacy 3.52px, /about 4.50px, HOMEPAGE HERO 8px -- the tail of the y in Qualify ended in a flat horizontal edge mid-stroke, visibly amputated. Only a LAST line can suffer it, which is why surveys of overflow, line-clamp and fixed heights all came back clean. Fixed with padding-block-end plus an equal negative margin, so the box grows for PAINT not for SPACE; proved layout-neutral, next element moves 0.000px. Now 0 missing everywhere.

(2) CALCULATOR: the maths was NEVER wrong. The result card rendered at y=889.5 in a 900px viewport, 1.99% visible; the legacy engine scrolled it into view and the Astro port dropped that line. issues.title: /crowmark/ hero proof card spills 35px and overlaps the row below

(1) The 35px is NOT content spill: it is exactly 4% at every width, which is the -4% in .duty__ghost, an aria-hidden decorative plane deliberately offset outward. .duty__face overflows by ZERO at all widths and the page never overflows. (2) The orphan does NOT overlap the row below: 17.9px clearance at 1440. The audit compared axis-aligned bounding boxes of ROTATED siblings, which always intersect. (3) The text is not 13px mono, it is Inter. REAL defects were the orphan line and legibility: a non-axis-aligned transform takes the subtree off the pixel grid, so a 400-weight glyph at --t-micro is about 1px of ink. Fixed with text-wrap balance (the site idiom, not a fourth recipe) and a size bump ONLY above 1100px where the card is actually tilted. Worst last-line fill 12% -> 50%. Trade-off stated: the rotation was kept and paid for in type, because the citation dates are what make the claim checkable and widening the card would put the page into horizontal overflow.

issues.title: Trade mark exposure: Microsoft and Google marks used without the required permission
issues.note: NOT an engineering call. Microsoft: a formal licence is generally required, the symbol and logotype must be used together (we use symbol only), and M365 app icons need a trademark licence. Three Microsoft marks are served and no licence is held. Entra ID is the correct current mark but comes from a pack whose terms exclude marketing use. Google: the G is for referring to Google the company, needs a co-branding arrangement for marketing, and must not sit on backgrounds that inhibit legibility, which our dark navy does. Recorded in LOGO-PROVENANCE.md, not silently fixed. Same class of risk as the Crowe trade mark remediation of July.

issues.title: Five vendor marks could not be sourced officially and were left in place
issues.note: RESOLVED with an ACCURACY rule, not a licence opinion: a mark is served only where it is the vendor OWN CURRENT mark for the product named beside it; otherwise the product is identified by name and the slot keeps the neutral dot. All six failed that test -- two drew the Microsoft CORPORATE symbol, one the Google G, three were retired generations. Re-check found more than no colour file: Ping brand-guidelines page now 404s; Microsoft states a third party MAY WRITE that its product works with Teams and MAY NOT use the icon; Workspace is not in Google logo list at all. Nothing informational was lost because both surfaces already print the product name in text. Entra ID and Google Drive DELIBERATELY excluded -- they are correct current artwork, so the accuracy rule does not reach them and mixing the two questions would make a withdrawal read as a legal opinion. Gate rule 3 added and proved both ways.

Proved by fresh export: git archive, npm ci twice, full chain, exit 0. THE EXPORT FOUND A DEFECT THE LOCAL TREE COULD NOT: check-status-pulse.mjs filtered astro-cid-, an ATTRIBUTE name that can never be a class, so after the class-scoping switch both live pulse marks went STALE while the local tree kept passing. Excluded with ignore rules: 2 stale homepage captures (opened and checked: public marketing pages, no account data) and 4 ad-hoc probes hard-coded to ports.

issues.title: .visually-hidden was FOURTEEN byte-identical copies under two names
issues.note: 13 scoped style blocks declaring .visually-hidden plus .sr-only in tokens.css. Every existing gate polices what a page PRESENTS, so the one class whose entire purpose is NOT to be presented forked in plain sight. Now one definition in tokens.css @layer utilities; 13 copies deleted, 7 call sites migrated. Gate is TWO halves because neither suffices: a source count cannot tell whether the definition WINS, and there is a recorded day when an unlayered margin:0 beat it and put four captions on the page. Both proved in both directions.

issues.title: The real cause of contiguous false failures is a SECOND concurrent build, not :8095
issues.note: Four full-chain runs failed with zero routes measured and passed seconds later on the same dist. Cause: astro build EMPTIES dist before writing, and every gate from step 9 reads dist, so a concurrent build empties it underneath the first. One run reported 24 CONSECUTIVE routes in alphabetical order with no main and 23 with no h1 -- the same contiguous-block signature previously attributed to :8095, produced here by the collision. Rule of thumb now written into check-render.js: a contiguous block of failures in ROUTE ORDER is the signature of the server or a neighbouring build, not of the site.

issues.title: Leaked code comment rendering as body text on /contact
issues.note: ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED IN SOURCE. contact.astro line 113 opens a JSX block comment; line 126 spelled the comment delimiters out LITERALLY inside the prose, and a block comment cannot nest, so that inner closing delimiter terminated the comment four lines early and everything after it rendered as body copy inside main. A note explaining a malformed-comment defect was itself malformed by the same mechanism it described. VERIFIED in the rebuilt dist AND on the served page: zero occurrences in both. The fix is to describe the delimiters in words rather than spell them out, and the incident is recorded in the comment itself so the next author does not repeat it.

issues.title: Blog list to footer dead space on /blog
issues.note: FIXED, and honestly qualified: "a large empty gap" does NOT reproduce. Measured 130.4px to footer against a sitewide norm of 91.5px on 31 of 43 routes -- 42% over, not multiples. Now 101.6px. Cause: the last register row contributed its own block padding as clearance for a rule that is never drawn, because the register rules go ABOVE rows. The residual 10.1px is the thumbnail standing taller than a two-line headline, which is content.

issues.title: FAQ inter-group spacing is far larger than the site rhythm
issues.note: FIXED: 171px to 85.5px at 1440, and exactly the 72px token floor on a short viewport at 390. The owner cited ~130px; measured 171. Cause: two section paddings back to back, a closing one and an opening one with nothing between them, against a ~60px rhythm inside the register. The closing "Still have questions?" seam deliberately KEEPS the full 171px because it stops answering and starts asking.

issues.title: Pricing card top content does not align across the three cards
issues.note: FIXED. Measured at 1440: plan names, sub-labels and prices ALL 40.4px out; now 0px on every row. At 834 the two-card band was 42.2px out, now 0. Cause: only Pro renders the badge, so under flex the other two simply started one element higher for the whole length of the card. RESERVED via subgrid, not absolute positioning: absolute needs the badge height written down plus a gap number, and both move the day the chip type changes. The row now reserves a track that is sized BY the card that has a badge, so height is reserved because a sibling needs it, not because somebody measured it. At 390 each card is its own band and nothing is reserved.

issues.title: Footer column headings are h3 at 12px
issues.note: FIXED, and it promoted the GROUP rather than demoting the label. A plain p alone fixes the outline but costs a screen-reader user four heading stops in the footer. Each column is now a nav landmark with aria-labelledby pointing at the visible text, so the accessible name IS the visible text by construction. Measured from the accessibility tree: before, four false level-3 headings beside real 32.8px ones; after, four navigation regions and zero false headings. .grouplabel untouched and the footer title now produces the SAME fingerprint as the mega-menu label, so no fifth recipe.

issues.title: About paired-column vertical alignment
issues.note: MISALIGNED, NOT CLIPPED -- and the distinction was worth measuring. Every ancestor computes overflow visible and no ancestor clips, so no ink is lost; the heading does paint 3px above its own border box because line-height 1.14 is tighter than the natural line box, but that lands inside 85.5px of section padding and is fully drawn. The real cause was align-items:center on .role__grid: the prose column is taller than the artefact card, so centring dropped the card and left the heading alone at the top. The section the owner named was the WORST of the four at 89.4px, which corroborates it. THE FIGMA RENDER SETTLED IT: all four frames put heading and artefact at a CONSTANT 8px offset on columns of unequal content, so a centre would have moved with the copy. align-items:center was an unrecorded departure from the design. Now start; delta 0.0px on all four rows.

issues.title: Homepage stat-card uneven height in Four numbers
issues.note: The report does NOT reproduce at 1440 -- all four cells measure 231.5px equal, and labels 1 AND 4 both wrap. It reproduces at 834 where the grid becomes 2x2: bands 200.2 vs 225px, a 24.8px difference from the fourth label taking two lines. Fixed with grid-auto-rows 1fr, one declaration with no number in it. STATED, not hidden: a one-line label beside a two-line one still leaves more air under the shorter, because labels sit at the top of their cells. The only lever left is the copy, and that copy is a sourced statutory label.

issues.title: Sub-44px tap targets in nav and footer
issues.note: MEASURED, NOT EDITED -- the fix belongs in Nav.astro which another agent held. TWO CORRECTIONS to the report: the links are 39.1px, not ~31px (31.3-33.3 is the WIDTH of FAQ, probably what got measured), and at 834 and 390 the nav is ALREADY fully 44px -- hamburger 44x44 and 0 of 16 mobile-menu elements under. Sub-44 targets exist only at 1025 and above, where input is a pointer. Exact change verified by injection: min-block-size 44px on .ca-nav-links > a and .ca-dropdown-trigger. NOT padding, because --t-body is fluid and a padding figure clearing 44px at 1440 measured 43.4px at 1025. Column width byte-identical, nothing visible moves. FOOTER measured and left: 31 of 31 links under 44px, 24 to 36px.

issues.title: Empty alt on all six homepage images
issues.note: SIX OF SIX CORRECTLY EMPTY; nothing changed. The six are integrations chip logos, and every chip renders logo then VENDOR NAME IN TEXT then scope in text, so alt text would make a screen reader say the name twice. The owner note guessed at the hero diagram: the drawn diagrams are NOT images -- spine, reasoning trace and both-sides rail are figures whose content is real list text with visually-hidden prefixes, and the lifecycle ring is inline SVG with role=img plus title and desc. All already correct; alt does not apply.

issues.title: Body line-height is browser default
issues.note: FIXED, and the scale was larger than it sounds: 3,002 elements rendered words at line-height NORMAL, which is a FONT METRIC -- measured in-browser at Inter 1.21, JetBrains Mono 1.32, Plus Jakarta Sans 1.33 -- so the site rhythm depended on which typeface an element happened to use. Base set on body. Two things it reached were fixed WHERE THEY ARE DECLARED rather than excluded: headings got their own --lh-heading, and two footer micro-labels state tight. Result diffed between two BUILT copies: +0.33% document height, header unchanged at 73px on every route, zero horizontal overflow, and NO heading grows at either width. Also closed a defect nobody chose: three heading sets were inheriting body leading from a card ancestor, 32.4px on a 20.9px heading.

issues.title: Only one fluid type rule; headings step by breakpoint
issues.note: NO CHANGE, because the premise does not hold in this build. tokens.css already contains 26 clamp() tiers and there is NOT ONE @media block setting a heading font-size anywhere in astro/src. Measured h1 across ten routes at four widths: 41.6 / 51.708 / 83.2 / 83.2 -- fluid between about 671 and 1342px and pinned outside, which is a clamp working. NO 73px h1 exists on any route at any width; the origin of that figure is UNVERIFIED and does not reproduce. Adding clamp here would mean re-tuning an existing clamp, i.e. a size change nobody asked for.

issues.title: About 15 of 60 interactive elements have no transition
issues.note: FIXED centrally with ONE edit: the pointer floor in motion.css lost its main scope, and its reduced-motion mirror with it -- a mirror narrower than the rule it mirrors is the duration-collapsed-but-displacement-stayed defect in reverse. Timing only, so no hover state changes appearance. Measured 10 signatures / 1,548 elements with no transition plus 5 signatures still animating under reduce, matching the audit roughly 15. THE GATE FOUND A DEFECT NOBODY ANTICIPATED: --dur-card was missing from the prefers-reduced-motion block in tokens.css, so 49 card links across 11 routes still reported 0.5s under reduce -- the displacement was already killed, what remained was the animation without the movement. Drawn-figure hovers argued for and left, and needed no exception because they are not in the floor selector list at all.

issues.title: Duplicate clear buttons in the glossary search field
issues.note: Kept the CUSTOM clear button and removed Chromium native cancel button, with reasons: the native control does not exist in Firefox, is not in the tab order, has no accessible name, and is a fixed ~13px square below the 24px floor that cannot be styled up. Custom raised 34 to 44x44. Also found the field reserving 52px of START padding for a search icon that does not exist.

issues.title: Blog post body flips to a light theme
issues.note: The article hero is dark and matches the site; the body flips to white with dark text, the only light surface on an otherwise fully dark site, with no bridging. The sticky header DOES adapt on scroll so nav links stay legible. Decision needed: theme the body dark, or make the transition deliberate so it reads as an intentional reading mode rather than a broken section.

issues.title: FAQ questions and answers are centre-aligned
issues.note: CLOSED by landing the two coupled edits together. .faq-item__a joins the read-rather-than-scanned set in alignment.css AND the BODIES constant that check-render.js MIRRORS BY HAND. The previous agent found the coupling by replaying the gate with only the stylesheet changed -- it failed on div.faq-item__a -- and correctly refused to ship half of it. The QUESTIONS stay centred deliberately: a summary here is a short label scanned across a ruled register, longest about 45 characters, none wrapping at 1440, so the read-rather-than-scanned argument does not reach them.

issues.title: Multi-column card content imbalance across three routes
issues.note: FIXED with a structural grid, not by balancing copy. New .card-sync in card-row.css hands each card the container tracks via subgrid, so every nth part is sized by the tallest nth part in the band. No number in the recipe; the only thing a call site declares is --card-parts, a fact about its markup, and the gate checks that against the RENDERED page rather than trusting it -- it caught a genuine mistake during development. Trailing slack across five bands: 231.1, 229.4, 54.6, 115.6 and 0 all to ZERO. HONEST LIMIT recorded in the file: where a card LAST part is a body paragraph this changes no pixel a reader sees; it fixes every row above the last.

issues.title: Billing toggle stays active on the For buyers pricing tab
issues.note: FIXED through the EXISTING switcher, not a second mechanism: tabs.ts gained one data attribute meaning this control only applies while these panels show. Applied to BOTH halves, the clipped input and the visible row, because they are several nodes apart and marking one would leave the other keyboard-reachable. Hiding is REAL, proven on dist: computed display none, rendered area 0, and the ARIA snapshot shows the node GONE on buyers. The hidden-beaten-by-display warning was live -- .billing { display:flex } is (0,2,0) once scoped and beats the UA rule. State is preserved, not reset.

issues.title: /tools H1 contradicts its title and intro
issues.note: THE TITLE WAS STALE, NOT THE H1 -- as suspected. /tools opened in May aggregating SIX tools; four went under the trade mark remediation in July and one separately, leaving exactly one directory on disk. The H1 and standfirst were written AFTER the withdrawals and were already true. Title and the ItemList name corrected to the singular; H1 untouched.

issues.title: jsTotal:0 and htmlPerRoute are in direct tension; only an ADR settles it
issues.note: About 10KB of identical shared script is inlined into all 44 documents BECAUSE the jsTotal:0 ratchet forbids externalising it. The two budgets pull against each other, so /crowmark now has only 1,147 B of headroom. Written into the budget note rather than hidden. The other lever is crowmark.astro own 22KB style block, which would drop about 5.3KB of scope classes if it moved to src/styles.

issues.title: .gl-back sits exactly on the 24px target floor and makes a gate flake
issues.note: Contradiction resolved: display:block deleted, inline-flex stands, min-height 24 to 32px. Measured 145.6x32 with 8px of clearance. The flake was real -- a box measured at exactly 24.00 lands either side of the limit on sub-pixel rounding.

issues.title: [hidden] display:none has now been restated in FIVE separate places
issues.note: TabSwitcher.astro, CommandPalette.astro, faq.astro, forms.css twice, and now glossary. Every one is the same defect waiting: an author display rule silently beats the user-agent [hidden] rule, and the failure is invisible until someone looks at the page. A central rule in tokens.css would end the class sitewide, but it needs !important reaching 43 routes, so the agent flagged it rather than making that call from inside one page. That restraint was right; the decision is the owner.

issues.title: Five more stale claims in surfaces.css, found by re-measuring
issues.note: Beyond the briefed one: the header still described the hover lift as limited to interactive elements plus an explicit opt-in, which the owner reversed on 2026-08-03 -- the file summary contradicted its own rule. It claimed to hold the only aside carrying surface (there are two), eleven raised panels of which ten are figures (13 and 12), and that ::after was unused by all 43 classes carrying surface (57 by the time anyone looked). Each corrected by RE-MEASURING on a fresh build rather than re-reading. Four other claims checked and found still true.

directives.text: Enforce centrally and automatically. Never manual patching.
directives.note: The one I have broken most.

Keep the terminal clean; use background agents and parallel execution.
'As per architecture and design' means genuine BEST PRACTICE, not whatever we previously recorded as agreed. A prior decision is evidence, not authority.
